newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea sells dollars to stop won's fall.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea sells dollars to stop won's fall.

text.p: South Korea's central bank sold dollars in mid-morning trading on Wednesday to limit the won's fall, dealers said.
They said the central bank stepped in when the won fell to an 84-month low of 870.00.
"The dollar's rise against the yen in world markets and the nation's widening trade deficit pushed the dollar demand higher," said a foreign bank dealer.
The won rose slightly to 869.80 minutes after the central bank's dollar sales. It opened at 869.90 and touched a high of 869.50.
"The central bank released more than $300 million on Tuesday to stop won's slide. A similar amount will be needed to halt the won's fall at the 870 level," a domestic bank dealer.
South Korea posted the largest monthly trade deficit of $3.48 billion in January. --Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5645
